transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-16 15:00 PST | Duration: ~62 mins | Attendees: Samira (Redwood AE), Jonah (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Maria (Acme Legal), David (CTO), Ethan (Infosec), Leah (Procurement)

00:00 Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I think we have a full agenda, MSA we're aware you circulated a version, DPA, SLA questions, and then pricing and onboarding. Quick round-robin — can folks say who they are?
00:12 Maria Rodriguez (Acme Legal): Hi everyone, Maria Rodriguez, legal counsel on Acme's vendor team. I'll be driving the redlines.
00:18 David Chen (Acme CTO): David Chen, CTO. I'm overseeing the technical and procurement side, will coordinate with Ethan for security.
00:23 Ethan Park (Acme Infosec): Ethan Park, Infosec. I'll be doing the security review.
00:26 Leah Ortiz (Procurement): Leah Ortiz, procurement — I'll shepherd PO and payment terms.
00:30 Samira: Great, thanks. Jonah and I will walk through outstanding items. Jonah, do you want to kick off on the security/SLA side?
00:36 Jonah (Redwood SE): Sure — thanks. So quick context: Redwood provides hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments. From the MSA/DPA perspective we typically offer the DPA as a standard addendum, SOC 2 Type II evidence available, and we support SSO/SAML, SCIM, RBAC, and KMS integrations. For dedicated and private we can do customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM.
01:05 Ethan: Quick clarifying Q — for private deployments, how does key management work? We need to ensure no plaintext customer data is accessible to Redwood operations.
01:14 Jonah: Good question. In private (VPC/on-prem) deployments, we support customer-managed KMS keys and HSM integrations so Redwood does not have access to unwrapped keys. For hosted API, we have envelope encryption and customer-managed keys are possible for some tiers; we'll confirm exact flows in the security pack.
01:34 Ethan: Okay, please send the architecture diagram for KMS flow. Also need audit logs: token-level usage, per-route logs, and per-request metadata.
01:44 Jonah: Yep, we can provide audit logs and per-route tracing. There's an option to retain logs in your S3 for X days — we can configure retention policies. We'll include sample log schema in the security docs.
01:58 Maria: On the MSA, a few headline items: liability cap, data residency clause, and DPA specifics around subprocessors. We circulated a redline but it's fairly conservative on our side. How flexible are you on liability cap and indemnity?
02:12 Samira: Thanks — we saw the redline. Liability caps we typically negotiate based on contract value and security posture. For enterprise procurements we have a staged cap approach with exceptions for gross negligence. We can propose language that aligns with your procurement thresholds. On subprocessors, Redwood uses a limited set of infra providers; we list them in the DPA and commit to notice if changes occur.
02:35 Leah: Payment terms — we prefer net 60 for enterprise buys. Pricing approval will go through our finance team; can you provide an example invoice and payment schedule?
02:45 Samira: Yes, we'll send a sample invoice and standard payment terms. We can be flexible with net 60 for annual committed Dedicated deals — need to route via finance but we can get that in a commercial redline.
02:58 David: SLA question — for our inference workloads, 99.95% uptime is minimum. What are your committed SLAs for Dedicated vs hosted? Also for latency SLOs, do you commit to p95/p99 numbers?
03:15 Jonah: For Dedicated we offer SLA-backed uptime targets — typical is 99.9% to 99.95% depending on the commit level. For hosted API we have different tiers; we can include latency SLOs for p95 under given payload sizes and model families. For deterministic p99 we often recommend Dedicated or Private so you can have reserved capacity. We'll share the SLA matrix.
03:36 Ethan: Are there credits for SLA misses? How are incidents measured — region-level or per-customer?
03:42 Samira: Yes, SLA credits are standard and are measured at the customer tenancy level. We'll include the exact credit formula in the SLA doc.
03:50 Maria: Back to the MSA redline — there's a clause on audit rights. We need at least annual audits or the right to request third-party SOC2 evidence. Is that available?
04:00 Jonah: We can provide SOC2 Type II reports and accommodate reasonable audit requests. For private deployments, you can run your own controls locally. We'll provide evidence and a point of contact for audits.
04:12 Maria: Great. Also need to confirm data deletion and data retention timelines in the DPA — especially for logs and KV cache.
04:20 Jonah: We'll include data retention options. For hosted, default retention is 30 days for logs and prompt data retention is configurable; for Dedicated/Private you control retention policies and cache eviction. We'll document exact endpoints to trigger data purge and support certificate for deletion on contract end.
04:44 Leah: For procurement timing — if legal signs off by 2026-03-25, can you onboard us by end of March? We have a product launch in early April.
04:54 Samira: Tight but possible. If legal returns redlines by 3/25 and we get PO quickly, we can aim for an onboarding kickoff week of 3/29 and rapid onboarding to production in the first week of April. Priya, is that feasible?
05:05 Priya (CSM): We can run a focused onboarding with a 2-week ramp — with Dedicated capacity it's faster. We'll scope a checklist and delivery timeline and send it after this call.
05:16 David: On the pricing spreadsheet — can you include both hosted per-token rates and Dedicated committed capacity pricing, and a sample cost projection for our estimated volume of 50M tokens/month? Also include quantized model options to reduce cost.
05:30 Samira: Absolutely, we'll include hosted and Dedicated pricing tiers, recommended quantization/throughput profiles, and a sample cost projection based on 50M tokens. We'll call out potential discounts for commit levels.
05:44 Ethan: A security nit — SSO via SAML plus SCIM for provisioning is required. We'll also need RBAC mapping to our AD groups. Can Redwood integrate with Okta?
05:54 Jonah: Yes, we support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning, and AD group sync to RBAC roles. Okta is supported. We'll attach the SSO config guide.
06:06 Maria: On subprocessors, one of our legal asks is a notification window before onboarding any new subprocessor. Can you commit to 30 days notice?
06:15 Samira: We can commit to notice windows for material changes; 30 days is reasonable for infra-provider changes. We'll verify specifics with ops but it's a standard ask we can meet.
06:28 Leah: PO/Procurement — do you accept net 60 and can you accept electronic PO? Also need your W-9 and corporate tax ID.
06:36 Samira: We accept electronic PO. We'll provide W-9, corporate details, and can accept net 60 depending on contract size — we'll flag finance.
06:45 Maria: A couple more technical questions — for private deployments do you support air-gapped installs? Some of our regulated teams require it.
06:53 Jonah: We offer an on-prem package that can be run in air-gapped mode; it requires some manual steps and a support package. We'll include the checklist and required migration windows.
07:06 David: For the benchmark Jonah mentioned, can we scope it to our 1) short-chat workloads (max seq 512, average 64) and 2) long-context summarization (max seq 8k)? We care about p95 latency for chat and throughput for long-context.
07:22 Jonah: Yes — we'll run both workloads. For long-context we can test both KV cache warm and cold start scenarios. We'll provide a simple harness and measurements for p50/p95/p99 plus cost per 1k tokens.
07:35 Samira: OK let's recap actions before we open to Qs. Samira will send pricing and T&Cs by 2026-03-18. Jonah runs perf bench and sends results. Maria to return legal redlines by 2026-03-25. Priya to propose onboarding kickoff dates. Ethan to send audit/log requirements by 2026-03-20. Any additions?
07:53 Maria: One request — can you also provide the list of subprocessors and a copy of your Data Processing Addendum (the current version)? We want to compare line-by-line.
08:01 Jonah: Yes, we'll attach current DPA and subprocessor list.
08:06 Leah: Also, any references for finance — we've had procurement questions about net terms for similar vendors. Do you have 2 reference customers we can contact?
08:15 Samira: We can provide references; I'll get permission and pass along two customers in a similar industry by next week.
08:22 David: Side note — competitors. We're also evaluating OpenAI and Vertex for hosted, but per our infra and data residency needs Dedicated/private is a differentiator for Redwood.
08:34 Samira: Totally — we understand. We'll make sure the perf and security docs show the differences.
08:40 Ethan: Last operational question — during onboarding who is the primary Redwood contact for escalations?
08:45 Priya: That's me (Priya Kumar), CSM, and we'll assign an SE (Jonah) for technical integrations and an ops contact. Priya's contact details will be in the kickoff invite.
08:56 Samira: Great. Any last questions?
09:00 Maria: None from legal right now. We'll review and come back with redlines.
09:04 David: No more from engineering.
09:06 Leah: I'll circulate internal procurement checklist after this call.
09:10 Samira: Thank you, everyone. We'll send the docs and pricing later today/tomorrow and follow up on next steps.
09:15 Meeting end.

Notes about transcript quality: Some words may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., KV cache spelled as K-V cache or misspelled), and there are occasional overlaps. The timestamps are approximate (every ~30-90 seconds).
